module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 376

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/376](https://www.erdosproblems.com/376)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos376

/--
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that ${2n\choose n}$ is coprime to $105$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_376 : answer(sorry) ↔ { (n : ℕ) | n.centralBinom.Coprime 105 }.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75] have shown that, for any two odd primes $p$ and $q$,
there are infinite many $n$ such that ${2n\choose n}$ is coprime to $pq$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_376.variants.prime {p q : ℕ} (h₁ : p.Prime)
    (h₂ : Odd p) (h₃ : q.Prime) (h₄ : Odd q) :
    { (n : ℕ) | n.centralBinom.Coprime (p * q) }.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos376

review.notes:
Both declarations faithfully express the independently corroborated mathematical claims. Direct access to https://www.erdosproblems.com/376 was blocked by Cloudflare despite a descriptive User-Agent; the exact main question was instead verified against OEIS A030979 and the introduction of arXiv:2201.11274v2, and the two-prime variant against EGRS75 and OEIS. The current Erdős-problem data table records problem 376 as open, consistent with the file; the variant is an established EGRS75 result.

Inspected the definitions and elaborated statements. Independent checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully without warnings. They establish that admitting n = 0 does not change infinitude, that the predicate for 105 means divisibility by none of 3, 5, 7, and that coprimality with p*q decomposes into coprimality with both factors. Allowing p = q is harmless and is covered by the primary paper's commensurable-base case. Prime/odd hypotheses are satisfiable and exclude 0, 1, and 2. Computed solutions for 0 ≤ n ≤ 1000 are exactly 0, 1, 10, 756, 757, matching OEIS. No mathematical or status discrepancies were identified.
